$comment: Canonical capture scenario for agy wire fixtures. captures/README.md is the runbook; this file is the single source of truth.
Array order is CAPTURE ORDER: capture-flow.mjs plan prints it and extract() assigns flows in this order (ambiguous slots resolve to the earliest unconsumed flow).
Slot names are load-bearing: tests/wire-parity.test.mjs and every captures/agy_cli_<version>/ directory pin them.
A new agy release must reproduce every slot not listed under dirs.<id>.omit. Drift is a test failure, never a judgement call.
dirs.<id>.patch overrides canonical fields for captures frozen before this manifest existed. Reasons are recorded, not fixed retroactively.

dirs.<id>.models remaps a canonical base-model pin to the generation that directory froze (legacy dirs predate the newest generation); the gate and the extractor apply it before matching, so a directory still has to match what it actually captured.

Coverage is per wire BRANCH, not per model id: the provider branches on family (sentinel injection, labels, thinking replay shape, quota pool) and on catalog facts (runtime id, enum, budget). gemini/claude/gpt each need at least one chain; a new model id inside a family needs no slot — the captured catalog plus the gate's Model Plan check cover id/tier/budget churn. A fourth family (or a new part shape) is a new branch and needs new slots.

observedEndpoints freezes agy's own startup surface beyond the five endpoints this provider implements. They are reference-only: the extractor writes them when present, the gate only checks that a present fixture has its counterpart, and nothing fails when a version stops sending one. Deliberately not frozen: oauth2/v2/userinfo and the avatar fetch (account PII), play.googleapis.com/log (telemetry).

Retention: only the current capture lives in the tree. Adding a version means deleting the previous captures/agy_cli_<version>/ directory (git history keeps it); dirs.<id> stays empty for that reason and is only populated when a capture must deviate from the canonical slots.

rules: Every `-c` run repeats --model: a bare -c silently resets to the default model (observed 1.1.28: a Claude session came back as gemini-3.7-flash-high).
One `agy -p <tool prompt>` yields a request chain (one request per tool round trip); the slots below name the ones to freeze.
Keep prompts trivial except where a slot says otherwise: quota is real and every extra turn costs it.
Never hand-edit a frozen fixture. Re-run the slot, or record the gap under dirs.<id> (omit/patch + reason).

prompts.ok: reply with exactly this one word: ok
prompts.done: reply with exactly this one word: done
prompts.tool: Create the file /tmp/agy-capture/notes.txt with exactly this content: Hello Antigravity. Then confirm it in one sentence.
prompts.reason: Think step by step, then answer in exactly one sentence: a train travels 120 km in 1.5 hours, what is its average speed in km/h?
prompts.readfail: Read the file /tmp/agy-no-such-file-xyz.txt and tell me its exact contents

endpoints.why: Browser-login authorize URL. Only appears when agy has no stored refresh token, so it needs a fresh login (README §2.1).
POST /token with grant_type=refresh_token: captured when the stored access token has expired.
Tier/project discovery, sent on every agy startup.
Model catalog snapshot the Model Plan resolves against (ADR-0008).
Quota Pool shape for the footer status.

observedEndpoints.why: agy startup (observed in 1.2.0): account-level admin gates. No provider counterpart — reference fixture.
agy startup: region + user settings. Reference fixture.
agy startup: server-driven experiment flags. Reference fixture.
Posted per tool trajectory in 1.2.0 ({trajectoryId}); empty response body. Reference fixture.

Third-party feature-flag client registration (POST, 202 with an empty body — the fixture's .resp.json is intentionally blank). Reference fixture; its machine-derived instanceId is redacted by the sanitizer.
Third-party feature-flag payload (GET, ~360KB). Reference fixture frozen for shape: the flags churn with every rollout, so a diff here is expected, not a wire change.

stream.why: Fresh tool turn. Its response (text + functionCall, ideally with a visible thought part: 1.1.26 showed 381 thoughts tokens) is the input to the turn2 divergence seam.

stream.divergence: agy drops the replayed thought part on a tool turn; this builder keeps it (wire-parity tool-turn seam test).
stream.why: Second request of the same invocation: the functionResponse envelope ({output}, role model). Its own stop reason is not pinned: the tool loop may answer (stop) or call another tool (toolUse) depending on how the model plans the same prompt.
Continuation of the tool session: replayed tool turns carry signatures, and a text-ending turn is what turn5 then replays.
The Turn Trace pair (ADR-0003) whose parser→builder seam is asserted: turn4's response must replay byte-identically.
Low leg of the effort matrix: runtime ID suffix + integer thinkingBudget (never -tiered/thinkingLevel).
Medium leg of the effort matrix.
Failed tool result: 1.1.26 embeds `Encountered error in tool execution: ...` in response.output with no `error` key.
Claude counter-capture (#14): thoughts arrive as thought:true parts, no thoughtsTokenCount.
Proves the Claude family replays thoughtSignature part-split too (signature on the visible text part, never on the thought part).
Second Claude continuation: used_claude/used_claude_conservative/used_non_gemini_model labels stay true across a chain.
Pro/agent runtime ID rename: the picker id gemini-3.1-pro must resolve to gemini-pro-agent + its enum and budget.
Gemini-family thinking replay outside flash: 1.1.28 turn10 returned a thought part, so this turn pins whether it replays like Claude's.

Third wire family. gpt-oss-120b is listed by the backend under exactly one variant (-medium, ADR-0009); the catalog carries thinkingBudget 8192. The command uses the bare id + --effort medium like the other families — agy models prints the variant id (gpt-oss-120b-medium), so flip the model field if the bare id is rejected.

The seam test turns this pair into strict evidence. 1.2.0 verdict: agy replays a gpt turn as plain text — turn12's 15 thought parts came back dropped, with no signature — so a gpt request has no reasoning history at all (unlike gemini and claude). src/builder.ts drops same-family gpt thinking to match. Probe E/F (pi_probe_sentinel) measured the other half on gpt-oss-120b-medium: an unsigned foreign functionCall is accepted (200) and the sentinel adds nothing (200), so this wire never needs ADR-0007's divergence.
